name: record-scaffolding-merge-limits
body: Five limits. (1) The merged files map is unioned and never pruned against the manifest, so a path deleted in an earlier scan can keep a later-retired module alive until a full-scan extraction replaces the record. (2) A pure-intermediate module with no files entry whose only parent module is retired survives as an orphan module with no parent edge until a full scan re-extracts; upgrade if the retirement walk must cascade through the stored Module-to-Module tree or prune stale file paths. (3) `record` reads the delta baseline `State` through a separate store open before it opens its write transaction, because loading while the write transaction holds `facts.lock` would self-contend for the bounded budget; the delta path therefore pays two store opens (~0.66 s on the 50k fixture); upgrade to a `FactStore`-taking `State::load_from` if the store ever forbids same-process double-open. (4) The delta refs upsert rests on `FactStore::refs` returning the whole stored map; an unreadable store yields an empty map and upserts every path - slower but not divergent; upgrade if a partially readable refs table ever becomes possible. (5) The record boundary no longer clears the intent or runs the collector: `cmd_scan` owns both after `run_pipeline` returns, so a contended clear waits up to the ~30 s writer-wait budget there, and the measured ingest-assembly window performs no whole-store collection; upgrade to a drop-guard for the intent if a scan's read/reuse phase could exceed `INTENT_GRACE_SECS`.
